masking_standard: Customer phone/account last-4 digits masked as **** in all shipped examples.

validated.where: iVUE account header — the working/billing number on the service order. Also in iVUE → Agreement + Account columns.
validated.note: Trailing IN / OUT / QDS marks the direction of the order (IN = connect, OUT = disconnect). Agreement types by prefix: bare NXX XXXX = phone, 101 = internet, 125 001 XXXX = EDGE. 559 is the area code (omit going forward). Exchanges: 822, 841, 855, 868, 877, 893. iVUE export cols: Agreement, Account.

validated.where: GET from LinePacks → the MGCP / endpoint name field (full provisioning string for the voice port). PUT in iVUE → Switch Equipment column (or New Switch Equipment on reassignment).
validated.note: Reads as: office (FRNT) – cabinet/tech (PRSV_GPON) – shelf CLX01 – slot 01 – port 04 – etc. MGCP is the Taqua protocol flavor. Same value as CSX/CRV/GR303 — different protocol names for the same switch-equipment box. If not populated in iVUE, look it up in LinePacks and update Switch Equipment. iVUE export cols: Switch Equipment, New Switch Equipment.

validated.where: GET from LinePacks → the GR303 / endpoint name field (full provisioning string for the voice port). PUT in iVUE → Switch Equipment column.
validated.note: Taqua provisioning for voice agreements. GR303 is the Taqua protocol flavor (alternate to MGCP). Same value as CSX/MGCP — different protocol names for the same switch-equipment box. If not populated in iVUE, look it up in LinePacks and update. iVUE export cols: Switch Equipment, New Switch Equipment.

validated.where: GET from LinePacks → Equipment, second column (the cabinet + card/slot/port identifier). PUT in iVUE → Equipment + Equip Desc columns.
validated.note: Second column on the equipment row — not the first. iVUE Equipment col holds the short name (e.g. ADT-N30-1-01); Equip Desc holds the cabinet prefix (e.g. ACRN-ADT). iVUE export cols: Equipment, Equip Desc.

validated.where: GET from LinePacks → Splitter view. Identifies the PON splitter shelf and port the customer rides. Also in iVUE → Equipment Name on 32X SPLITTER records.
validated.note: S = splitter number, P = port number on that splitter. iVUE export shows splitter records under Equip Type '32X SPLITTER' (e.g. MLTN-E1, MLTN-S1). iVUE export col: Equipment Name (on SPLITTER type records).

validated.where: GET from iVUE → Cable Name column (the distribution cable + count/pair the service runs on) OR from Fiberbook (G:\GIS_Projects). On new installs Fiberbook/as-built may have it before iVUE; on existing service iVUE is populated.
validated.note: Cable identifier followed by the pair/fiber count (e.g. ABRY-ACRN, BGCK-1). Pair number in adjacent Pair column. Cable Type column shows Copper/Fiber/Hybrid. iVUE export cols: Cable Name, Pair, Cable Type.

validated.where: GET from Fiberbook (G:\GIS_Projects) or the as-built drawing → MST and pedestal call-outs for the address. Also in iVUE → Serving Ped Parent Equip Name column. On new fiber installs Fiberbook/as-built is the source; on existing service iVUE has it.
validated.note: MST = Multi-Service Terminal (fiber tail); PED = Pedestal (copper/hybrid housing). Cross-check the as-built against Fiberbook when they disagree. iVUE export: Serving Ped Parent Equip Name (e.g. ACRN-109-5), Serv Ped Mstr Equip Cat (PED = pedestal).

validated.where: iVUE → Serving Ped Parent Equip Name column — the pedestal/housing the home is fed from.
validated.note: The physical equipment feeding the premises. Format varies: WIRE_CENTER-ID (e.g. ACRN-109-5) for copper peds, AHnnnn-n for aerial housings. iVUE export cols: Serving Ped Parent Equip Name, Serv Ped Desc (short name).
validated.data_confirmed: pattern AHnnnn-n / WC-nnn-n pedestals in data (AH203-1, AH1620-3)

validated.term: Parent Equipment — Internet line item / ONT SN
validated.where: iVUE → parent equipment under the Internet line item → ONT serial / FSAN field. GET from warehouse (new install) or Diana in Customer Care (ONT/modem assignment). PUT in iVUE → Equipment Name on ONT records (ONT-CXNK... prefix); also in Serial column.
validated.note: FSAN = the ONT serial identifier (e.g. CXNK0028C0E1). Often blank until the ONT is registered — Warehouse or Diana provides the serial. In iVUE export: Wire Center = ONT, Equipment col = the FSAN, Equip Type = Calix 711GE / 803G etc. iVUE export cols: Equipment Name (ONT-prefixed), Equipment, Serial.

validated.where: iVUE → service order header; the SO# (a related/grouped order may list several). In the note, written as SO# NNNNNN at the top.
validated.note: Format: 6-digit number. Multiple SO#s can appear when orders are bundled.

validated.where: iVUE → order date; written at the head of the note.
validated.note: Standard format: M.D.YY (going-forward standard for automation). Style JF writes it with slashes (8/1/23).

validated.where: Notes → the work being done, summarized at the top of the note after the date. Built from a controlled vocabulary of action codes.
validated.note: Drives which workflow/variant applies. Read left to right — each code adds meaning: DISC (disconnect, defaults TEL) · DISC TEL · DISC DSL · DISC TEL (CBOL) = phone removed, internet stays · RECON · CONN (+ QDS/speed/FTTH) · QDS (911-only dialing rules) · VACA (DISC=leaving, RECON=returning) · NPD (non-pay disc) · INT Upgrade to <speed> (+BND/SNGL/ADSL/VDSL/FTTH) · CBOL · Billing Correction · Correcting Service Points = provide 911 line# and address. Example: DISC TEL (CBOL), QDS CONN, & Billing Correction = remove phone (internet stays) + connect 911-only + fix billing.

validated.where: iVUE → FACS subsystem. After edits, record whether port/pair records were left alone, updated, or removed. Use one of the standard values — do not append tech initials or context.
validated.note: Standard values: No FACS Changed / FACS Updated / FACS Removed / FACS Corrected / FACS Cleared / No FACS Listed / FACS Reverted / FACS Pending. Bonding issues and context notes go in the note body, not here.

validated.where: iVUE → Agreement column. The number/phone agreement being disconnected or removed (the OUT line on a QDS swap, DISC, NPD, or MOVE).
validated.note: Format: NXX XXXX. (559) area code optional/omit going forward. Exchanges: 822, 841, 855, 868, 877, 893. iVUE export col: Agreement.

validated.where: iVUE → Agreement column. The number/phone agreement being connected or added (the IN line on a QDS swap, CONN, RECON, MOVE, or new service).
validated.note: Format: NXX XXXX. (559) area code optional/omit going forward. Exchanges: 822, 841, 855, 868, 877, 893. iVUE export col: Agreement.

validated.where: iVUE → Agreement column / QDS → the QDS-mapped number tied to the service swap. A new phone agreement assigned when connecting QDS — different number from the TEL being removed (OUT).
validated.note: Quick Dial Service for 911. In the note: NXX XXXX QDS IN. Format NXX XXXX, (559) optional. Exchanges: 822, 841, 855, 868, 877, 893. iVUE export col: Agreement.

validated.where: iVUE → Account column. The internet/EDGE billing account for the OUT number being disconnected or removed.
validated.note: Internet account number — non-telephone prefix indicates internet. Format: 101 NXX XXXX (internet) or 125 001 XXXX (EDGE). iVUE export col: Account.

validated.where: iVUE → Account column. The internet/EDGE billing account for the IN number being connected or staying.
validated.note: Internet account number — non-telephone prefix indicates internet. Format: 101 NXX XXXX (internet) or 125 001 XXXX (EDGE); often '101 NXX XXXX Stays'. iVUE export col: Account.

validated.where: Notes → the technician who wrote/completed the note; initials at the end of the date line (and the tech signature on its own line at the very end).
validated.note: Standard signature format: -XX- (dash-initials-dash), own line. Also your style selector — known: CT, JF, KM. Each tech's initials map to their writing style.

validated.where: GET from LinePacks → the voice port string for the *TEL section (switch-cabinet-shelf-slot-port + pair). Also in iVUE → Equipment Name + Port columns. LinePacks is the provisioning source; iVUE holds the service record.
validated.note: First token after *TEL. Three formats: FRNT-NNNN-NNNN (copper, 75%), FRNT-xxx-ADTnn (ADSL terminal, 13%), FRNT-xxx-CLXnn (GPON/fiber, 11%). Followed on the next line by TEL Location. iVUE export cols: Equipment Name (full), Port (short), Port Status.

validated.where: GET from LinePacks → first column (Equipment) the data port string for the *DSL section. Also in iVUE → Equipment Name + Port columns.
validated.note: First token after *DSL. Same formats as TEL Port (copper / ADSL / GPON). iVUE export cols: Equipment Name (full), Port (short), Port Status.

validated.where: LinePacks → any additional port not under TEL/DSL (cross-connect, secondary line). Also in iVUE → Equipment Name + Port columns.
validated.note: Catch-all for an extra port line. For bonded service, the two physical legs use Leg 1 / Leg 2 instead (see those terms). iVUE export cols: Equipment Name, Port.

validated.where: GET from LinePacks → the first bonded leg, labeled 'Leg 1' in the note. Also in iVUE → Equipment Name + Port columns. On moves/QDS, the OUT/old leg also appears here.
validated.note: Bonded service uses two legs (Leg 1 + Leg 2). Each leg has a port line then a location line, same structure as TEL/DSL. iVUE export cols: Equipment Name, Port.

validated.where: GET from LinePacks → the second bonded leg, labeled 'Leg 2' in the note. Also in iVUE → Equipment Name + Port columns.
validated.note: Bonded service uses two legs. Leg 2 in the note. iVUE export cols: Equipment Name, Port.

validated.where: GET from iVUE → FACS subsystem → the cable/pair + binding-post (cable tie-down) location for the TEL port. Also in iVUE → Serving Ped Parent Equip Name + Serv Ped Desc columns.
validated.note: BP = binding post (the cable tie-down point). The line after the TEL port in the note. iVUE export cols: Serving Ped Parent Equip Name, Serv Ped Port, Serv Ped Desc.

validated.where: GET from iVUE → FACS subsystem → the cable/pair + binding-post (cable tie-down) location for the DSL port. Also in iVUE → Serving Ped Parent Equip Name + Serv Ped Desc columns.
validated.note: BP = binding post (the cable tie-down point). The line after the DSL port in the note. iVUE export cols: Serving Ped Parent Equip Name, Serv Ped Port, Serv Ped Desc.

validated.where: Notes → the field-splicing instruction block (PIC extend / spliced-through call-outs). References cable/pair from iVUE Cable Name + Pair columns and Fiberbook.
validated.note: Flag for the splicer. Review against Fiberbook. Not stored as a field in iVUE — lives only in the note text.

validated.where: EDGE system → customer ID for EDGE FTTH product (always 125-001-XXXX). Also in iVUE → Account column with 125 prefix.
validated.note: Format: 125 001 XXXX. Agreement types: bare = phone, 101 = internet, 125 = EDGE. iVUE export col: Account (125-prefixed records).

validated.where: iVUE → combined switch/cable/port assignment string (Switch Equipment column). GET from LinePacks → switch-equipment (CRV) box; PUT in iVUE.
validated.note: Same value as MGCP/GR303 — different names for the same switch-equipment box. Sometimes appears short (e.g. 328-1345). If not in iVUE, look it up in LinePacks and update. iVUE export cols: Switch Equipment, New Switch Equipment.

validated.where: GET from LinePacks → the GPON upstream port for a fiber ONT. Also in iVUE → Equipment Name + Port on GPON equip-type records.
validated.note: FTTH only. Format: WLDF-ADT-N52-1-14-GPON-B-1. iVUE export: Equip Type = GPON, Equipment Name = full string, Port = GPON-B-1.

validated.where: EDGE system → the FTTH downstream port + pair for EDGE service. Also in iVUE → Equipment Name on EDGE records.
validated.note: EDGE product only; rare. Format: EDGE-MLTN-FTTH PORT-D-30 PAIR 30.

validated.where: Notes metadata → which monthly file the note came from. '… Line Assignments' = a Service Order; '… Tech Calls' = a trouble/tech-call note.
validated.note: Tech Calls run longer and usually log a field correction. Not stored in iVUE — metadata from the source document.

validated.where: Derived from the action phrase → the classified action pattern for the order (top workflow in the corpus).
validated.note: Big buckets: DISC_QDS_RECON, VACA_RECONNECT, DISCONNECT_ONLY, UPGRADE_*, NPD. Not a field in iVUE — derived from the action code combination.

validated.where: Notes → on a tech-call note, the 'Per <name>' tag crediting who directed the field change.
validated.example: Per Bart, wound up using pr 1613 on cable 2
validated.note: Frequent names: SE, Han, Kong, Tammie. Marks a same-SO correction, not a new order. Not stored in iVUE — lives only in the note text.

validated.where: Notes + FACS → tech-call language showing the originally-assigned port was changed in the field. The corrected port then updates iVUE → Switch Equipment and FACS records.
validated.note: Signals BAD_PORT_UPDATE: the SO port did not work, FACS was updated to the real one. iVUE and LinePacks can disagree — techs note e.g. 'marked bad in LinePacks but not in iVUE'.

suggested.note: Order classification (CONN, DISC, etc). iVUE export/grid col: SO Type.

suggested.where: iVUE → SO grid → SO Status column.
suggested.note: Lifecycle state of the order. iVUE grid col: SO Status.

suggested.where: iVUE → SO grid → Hold SO flag / Office Information → Hold SO checkbox.
suggested.note: Marks an order on hold (e.g. Beasore order put in hold pending engineering).

suggested.where: iVUE → SO → Workflow tab → task seq 19.0. The Engineering Facilities task — the GIS/facility-assignment step.
suggested.note: THIS IS CODY'S TASK in the SO workflow chain. Status QUEUE until worked, then COMP. Appears as alert E.FACS(1). Complete via right-click → Complete or Continue Workflow.

suggested.where: iVUE → Workflow tab → task seq 20.0. Programming — switch provisioning step after E.FACS.
suggested.note: Next task after E.FACS. Some orders route here (P:PROG) after facilities.

suggested.where: iVUE → SO → Workflow tab → ordered task list (Task / Task Seq / Critical / Priority / Needed / Current Status).
suggested.note: The full 27-task SO lifecycle. Prefixes: C=Customer Service, N=NOC/Network Ops, I=Internet Dept, E=Engineering(GIS), P=Programming/Provisioning. E.FACS (19) is GIS. Each task has a sequence number and status (COMP/QUEUE).
suggested.data_confirmed: iVUE Workflow-tab screenshot (UI reference); P.PROG/E.FACS also in pairs (52/12x)

suggested.where: iVUE → SO action bar → Continue Workflow button. Advances the SO to the next task after completing E.FACS.
suggested.note: How you hand the SO off after finishing facilities. Also Review SO, Validate/Close, Void, Print, Create SO on the same bar.

suggested.where: LinePacks → _LinePacks1 table → the exact column headers.
suggested.example: Switch | Equipment | Status | Voice Agreement | Data Agreement | Line/BP | Card Type
suggested.note: Confirmed from the _LinePacks1 Access table. Switch=CSX, Equipment=node/card/port, Line/BP=binding post. Search via Ctrl+F in the relevant column.

suggested.where: LinePacks → _LinePacks1 → Voice Agreement column. The phone agreement tied to a port.
suggested.note: Pairs the physical port to the voice (TEL) agreement. iVUE side = Agreement. Export already masks to prefix-only (matches our **** standard).
suggested.data_confirmed: LinePacks export (col: 'Voice Agreement / left only the prefix') + _LinePacks1 screenshot

suggested.where: LinePacks → _LinePacks1 → Data Agreement column. The internet agreement tied to a port.
suggested.note: Pairs the physical port to the data (DSL/internet) agreement. iVUE side = Account. Export already masks to prefix-only.
suggested.data_confirmed: LinePacks export (col: 'Data Agreement / left only the prefix') + _LinePacks1 screenshot

suggested.where: LinePacks → _LinePacks1 → Card Type column (last column). The manufacturer/model of the card the port lives on.
suggested.note: Determines bonding compatibility — both bonded legs must share card type. Adtran vs Calix rules apply.

suggested.where: Splitter turn-up response → FEEDER section. The backbone leg from GPON cabinet to the FDP.
suggested.note: Top section of a splitter turn-up. Cabinet GPON port to Fiber Distribution Point. BNDL = the cabinet/site prefix.

suggested.where: Splitter turn-up response → the FDP cross-connect (FDP-IN >> FDP-OUT).
suggested.note: Middle leg: the FDP cross-connect mapping in to out. BNDX = cross-connect point.

suggested.where: Splitter turn-up response → DISTRIBUTION section. Splitter port out to the MST port at the pedestal.
suggested.note: Bottom leg: splitter port to distribution cable/pair to MST port + AH pedestal. (3X5) = splitter ratio context.

suggested.where: Fiber Distribution Point — the cross-connect housing between feeder and distribution fiber.
suggested.note: Where feeder fiber cross-connects to distribution. Has IN and OUT pair positions.

suggested.where: The GPON cabinet/site prefix in fiber strings (e.g. BNDL = Bandit/site cabinet).
suggested.note: Site-cabinet identifier prefixing GPON and splitter strings. Pairs with a wire-center splitter (e.g. CKSD).

suggested.where: The procedure + response for bringing a new fiber splitter into service (new FTTH area).
suggested.example: Corning Dual 1X16 splitter, SFP 100-05148, UPCSC/SC SM DX 2M
suggested.note: Documents equipment installed (splitter, SFP, jumpers) plus the full FEEDER/X-CONNECT/DISTRIBUTION fiber path. Picked up from warehouse, logged in note.

suggested.where: \\ptc27\Drawings\DataPortal\LinkedDocs\GIS\Sites\ — per-site folder index mapping wire center → site name → exchange.
suggested.note: Maps codes to FTTH developments: TSVJ=Tesoro Viejo, MRBL=Mira Bella, PRSV=Friant Preserve, RNSE=Renaissance, CRES/LCRS=Cressman, SNRK=Sunrock, WLDF=Wildflower, DTON=Downtown O'Neals, etc. Also holds PTC FiberBook.xlsx, FRNT CLX ONT CRV Pool.txt, Calix_MGCP_PON_Construction.png.

suggested.where: iVUE → Query Builder → Category=Service Points, View='Service Point - Facilities with Serv Addr Status'. Filter to find subscribers/facilities.
suggested.note: How to pull all service points on a cable or in an area. Configure Columns / Load / Save / View SQL / Max Rows. Returns Serv Address City, Service Address, Tax Zone, Wire Center, SP Description, SP Remarks.

suggested.where: iVUE → Query Builder / Service Point result → Tax Zone column.
suggested.note: Tax jurisdiction for the service point. Appears in subscriber query results.

suggested.where: iVUE → Service Point → Wire Center column. The serving wire-center code.
suggested.note: 4-letter wire-center/CLLI code identifying the serving office. Drives equipment lookup.
suggested.data_confirmed: iVUE subscriber-query screenshot (col) + GIS Sites map

suggested.where: NewNet CMS → SQL view [NewNetCMS].[dbo].[IVUE_CablePair_Facs_Copper]. The copper cable/pair/facility join used for cutsheets.
suggested.note: 47-column view joining cable pair to facility/cross-connect/binding-post. Cols include XConn Cable Nm, MinSvPt_BP, Port_BP, bnd_pair, xconpair, CBOL, Cat Item, SubDown/SubUp. Used to build cutsheets.

suggested.where: Request → RECAP section. The switch-feature summary for the programming team (blocking, PIC, publish status).
suggested.example: RECAP: ALL BLOCKS, NO PIC, NON PUBLISHED
suggested.note: Recapture of switch features. Handled by P.PROG (programming), not E.FACS — but read it to understand the order. Common: NO PIC, COMPLETE/SELECTIVE block, NP (non-published), 900/COLLECT/3RD/INT'L blocks.

suggested.where: RECAP → no Preferred Interexchange Carrier (no long-distance carrier).
suggested.note: Customer has no toll/long-distance carrier. Opposite of a PIC assignment.

suggested.where: RECAP → number not listed in the directory.
suggested.note: Directory suppression. Shows as Nonpublish on the iVUE SO header.

suggested.where: RECAP → complete caller-ID blocking (number always shows PRIVATE).
suggested.note: vs Selective (SEL) where the number does appear. Caller-ID presentation control.

suggested.where: Request flag → order needs engineering/GIS design before facilities (drop placement, field meet).
suggested.note: Triggers a field meet / drawing / WO before the SO can be completed. Common on Beasore and new-area orders. Order often put in Hold.

suggested.where: Request → Assessor's Parcel Number for the property (used for vicinity maps / drop placement).
suggested.note: Parcel identifier. Looked up in ParcelQuest for EDGE/new-service inquiries and drop placement.

suggested.where: Response → field work order number for drop placement / construction.
suggested.note: Construction/field WO referenced in the response when a drop or plant work is dispatched.
